'''Nizam al-Din Hasan al-Nisaburi''', whose full name was '''Nizam al-Din Hasan ibn Mohammad ibn Hossein Qumi Nishapuri''' (d. 1328/29) ({{langx|fa|نظام الدین حسن نیشاپوری}}) was a [[Persian people|Persian]] [[Sunni]]{{sfn|Bosworth|Asimov|1992|p=105}}<ref name="Eid">{{cite web |last1=Eid |first1=Ali |title=الإمام نظام الدين النيسابوري .. غرائب القرآن ورغائب الفرقان |url=https://www.albayan.ae/sports/2005-10-15-1.107787 |website=[[Al-Bayan (newspaper)|Al-Bayan]] |publisher=Dubai Media Incorporated |access-date=30 January 2023 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20210710030717/https://www.albayan.ae/sports/2005-10-15-1.107787 |archive-date=10 Jul 2021 |page=|trans-title=Imam Nizam al-Din al-Nisaburi .. Curiosities of the Qur’an and Ragh’ib al-Furqan |language=ar |date=15 October 2005}}</ref>{{sfn|Al-Dhahabi|1997|pp=231{{ndash}}236}} Islamic [[Shafi'i]], [[Ash'ari]] scholar, mathematician, astronomer, jurist, Qur'an exegete, and poet.

==Family and education==
Nizam al-Din Hasan al-Nisaburi, who according to [[genealogical]] information provided in his full name—Nizam al-Din Hasan ibn Mohammad ibn Hossein Qumi Nishapuri—had a grandfather from the city of [[Qom]], was born in [[Nishapur]].{{Citation needed|date= May 2018}}

Little is known about Nīsābūrī's early life and education.{{sfn|Morrison|2007}} His early education was in the city of Nishapur, but he later moved to [[Tabriz]], the capital of [[Il-Khanids]] at the time.{{Citation needed|date= May 2018}}

Nīsābūrī studied under and worked with [[Qutb al-Din al-Shirazi]],{{sfn|Morrison|2007}} who was himself a student of [[Nasir al-Din Tusi]]. He was one of the great scientists of [[Maragheh observatory]].{{Citation needed|date= May 2018}}

In 1304, Nīsābūrī arrived in Azerbaijan; by 1306 he was in Tabrīz, the largest city in Azerbaijan.{{sfn|Morrison|2007}}

Nīsābūrī died in 1329/1330, the year he completed his {{transliteration|ar|Gharāʾib}}.{{sfn|Morrison|2007}}

== Works ==
===Astronomy and mathematics===
[[File:Nizam al-Din Hassan bin Husayn Qumi Nishapuri, known as Nizam-i a'raj (fl. 1311); a commentary on Tusi’s al-Tadhkirah Fi 'ilm al-Hay'a, signed ‘Ali bin Sufi bin Ibrahim Aqhari, Timurid Iran, dated December 1490.jpg|thumb|left|Manuscript of al-Nishaburi's commentary on [[Nasir al-Din Tusi]]'s ''Fi 'ilm al-Hay'a''. Copy created in Timurid Iran, dated December 1490]]

Nīsābūrī started to write {{transliteration|ar|Sharḥ Taḥrīr al‐Majisṭī}} ({{lang|ar|تفسیر التحریر}}, "Commentary on the recension of the Almagest") in 1303., a commentary on a work by [[Nasir al-Din al-Tusi]]. Together with an explanation al-Tusi's text, Nīsābūrī added his own results and ideas. He included data about the [[obliquity of the ecliptic]] and discussed the possibility that the [[Astronomical transit|transits]] of [[Venus]] and [[Mercury (planet)|Mercury]] across the Sun had been seen.{{sfn|Morrison|2007}}

Nīsābūrī second astronomical work, {{transliteration|ar|Kashf‐i ḥaqāʾiq‐i Zīj‐i Īlkhānī}} ("Uncovering the Truths of the Īlkhānid Astronomical Handbook") was completed in 1308/1309. A commentary on a {{transliteration|ar|zīj}} by Ṭūsī', it focused upon topics discussed in the {{transliteration|ar|Sharḥ}}, such as the positions of the planets in the night sky.{{sfn|Morrison|2007}}

{{transliteration|ar|Tawḍīḥ al‐Tadhkira}} (({{lang|ar|توضیح الذکر}}), "Elucidation of the Tadhkira") was a commentary on Ṭūsī's {{transliteration|ar|al‐Tadhkira fī ʿilm al‐hayʾa}} ("Memento on Astronomy") that investigated topics that included alternatives to [[Ptolemy]]'s model of the cosmos, and ideas to explain that accounted the known variations in the obliquity of the ecliptic.{{sfn|Morrison|2007}}

The {{transliteration|ar|Sharḥ}} and the {{transliteration|ar|Tawḍīḥ}} were not written for astronomers, but for students whose [[curriculum]] included astronomy.{{sfn|Morrison|2007}}

Nisaburi also wrote a [[treatise]] on mathematics.

===Religious works===
Nīsābūrī's most famous work is his {{transliteration|ar|[[Ghara'ib al-Qur'an wa Ragha'ib al-Furqan]]}} ({{lang|ar| تفسير النيسابوري‎}}, "A Commentary on the Wonders of Quran in Exegesis"), also known as {{transliteration|ar|Tafsir al-Nisaburi}}). It is {{transliteration|ar|[[tafsir]]}} of the [[Qur'an]], which closely follows [[al-Fakhr al-Razi]]'s {{transliteration|ar|tafsir}} in many places. The work was written to demonstrate the importance of science for religious scholars. The work reflects Nīsābūrī's scientific background, in contrast with Rāzī's bias towards the theologians.{{sfn|Morrison|2007}}

Nīsābūrī's other religious works include:
* {{transliteration|ar|Owqaf al-Quran}} ({{lang|ar|اوقاف القران}});
* {{transliteration|fa|Kashf-i Haqayeq-i Zij-i ilkhani}} ({{lang|fa|کشف حقایق زیج ایلخانی}}, "Explanation of the Facts"), an explanation of {{transliteration|ar|[[Zij-i Ilkhani]]}} by Nasir al-Din Tusi, written in [[Persian language|Persian]]
* {{transliteration|ar|Al-Basaer fi mukhtasar tanqih al-Manazer}} ({{lang|ar|البصائر فی مختصر تنقیح المناظر}}), a work on the topics in al-Manazer by [[Ibn Haytham]];
* {{transliteration|ar|Sharh on al-Shafia by Ibn Hajib}} ({{lang|ar|شرح نظام بر الشافیه}});
